principles: Fail closed on semantic scope drift
Use one canonical artifact registry and one composite digest
Separate scope-defining inputs from closeout-evidence outputs
Preserve existing lifecycle behavior unless a structured fact proves safe retention
drivers: Avoid synthetic TEST rollback for canonical closeout writes

options.name: A: Shared closeout trust module consumed by lifecycle and freshness gates
pros: Mechanical reuse across handlers and tests

options.name: B: Add local checks independently in each existing gate
cons: Harder to prove closed-set writer provenance

chosen: A: Shared closeout trust module consumed by lifecycle and freshness gates
rationale: The milestone exists to establish a mechanical trust boundary. A shared module gives schema/hash verification and the composite digest one authoritative implementation, while registries and contract tests prove every consumer uses it.

preMortem.scenario: Canonical TEST rollup still forces DEV/REVIEW
preMortem.trigger: Closeout artifact remains classified as scope-defining material
preMortem.mitigation: Positive TEST regression with unchanged composite digest and product diff.

preMortem.scenario: Semantic scope change is incorrectly retained
preMortem.trigger: Composite digest omits acknowledgement provenance, milestone ledger, or slice plan
preMortem.consequence: Old review evidence is reused after meaningful scope drift
preMortem.mitigation: Independent mutation case for each composite component and fail-closed missing component.

preMortem.trigger: Readers accept embedded ledgerHash/planHash/rollupHash without recomputation
preMortem.mitigation: Schema validate and recompute every trusted embedded hash before classification.

preMortem.scenario: New review round inherits old passes
preMortem.trigger: Retention key ignores reviewRound or signed re-attestation
preMortem.mitigation: Regression enters a new round and requires explicit current signed evidence.

preMortem.scenario: B-9188 conflict causes duplicate registry ownership
preMortem.trigger: Both stories edit milestone-closeout registration concurrently
preMortem.consequence: Merge conflict or contradictory process facts
preMortem.mitigation: Exclude that exact path until B-9188 merges; merge main before DONE and consume its result.
